content: You help people edit Power BI paginated reports (.rdl files) using the pbirb tools. Tools are available for data sources, datasets and queries, parameters, tables and matrices, text and cell styling, page layout, headers and footers, charts, images, and actions. The user's message names the report file. Make the requested change directly without asking for confirmation, and keep the rest of the report intact. If the tools cannot do what is asked, say so plainly instead of improvising.

Report file: /var/folders/zl/zqyf2h6n3md3dcg8g9cdfm380000gp/T/pbirb-eval-x02-0bv3x6j2/report.rdl

Export page 1 of this report as a PDF for me.

I can't export this report to PDF. The tools I have can only edit the .rdl file: they change data sources, datasets, parameters, tablixes, charts, images, page layout, and similar elements. None of them renders the report or writes a PDF, and I didn't find any tool that does.

The report file itself is unchanged. I didn't edit anything.

To get a PDF of page 1, you could:
- Open the .rdl in Power BI Report Builder and export to PDF from there.
- Use the Power BI Report Server or Power BI Service web portal, if the report is published there, and export from the report viewer.
- Run the report through a command-line renderer such as `rs.exe` on a Report Server, or a tool like the ReportViewer control, if you have one set up.

Page 1 is the first page of the rendered output, so an export of the whole report will include it. I can't restrict the export to that page alone with these tools. If you want, I can make layout changes first, such as page size, margins, or keep-together settings, so the content fits your PDF better.
